analysis:
Only documentation and a changelog entry changed; no source code is in this batch. changelog.d/nemotron-super-video-body-bound.md (lines 3-5) states Nemotron 3.5 Super media request bodies are now accepted up to 40 MiB (previously 8 MiB). Bodies above the bound fail as `media_too_large` instead of `invalid_media`. The worst-case media charge for capacity quotes grows to 4.67 GiB per image, 4.54 GiB per video and 25.6 GiB for sixteen images. docs/architecture/hardware-support.md lines 51-59 (head) mirror these figures, and the date stamp moved to 2026-10-23.

Security relevance: the implementation (NemotronSuperServingPolicy.mediaChargeBytes, the ingress body check) is outside the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify that the 40 MiB bound is enforced before decode/allocation or that memory charging matches the documented figures. Availability considerations (TB-007, T-016, T-029 class) are relevant: a consumer could send larger bodies, but the documented design charges the full media reservation against the process ledger before admission, and a 16-image request is documented as not fitting on 128 GB. No observed regression is evidenced in the supplied text. Threat-model entries on media plaintext (T-050) are not affected by documentation alone.

The next pass should confirm in the code that (1) the 40 MiB limit applies per part and per request across all transports, (2) the charge is taken before decode, and (3) the `media_too_large` error path leaks no plaintext. Neither the A-001 prompt confidentiality assets nor the coordinator/provider encryption boundaries are touched by these files.
